Kaneki Auth data model

Every table in one app's database, what each column means, and which flow writes it.

  • Updated2026-11-10
  • Better Auth1.7.19
  • Scopeone app's Neon project
  • Companionuse cases · flows · architecture

The data model in one page

Short answer

Each app's Neon database holds 14 tables: 4 core Better Auth tables (with admin-plugin columns added), 7 OAuth-provider tables, and one each for API keys, signing keys and rate limits. Everything hangs off user and oauthClient. Every app gets an identical, separate copy. S1S2S3

4core tables
7OAuth provider tables
3keys, JWKS, rate limit
1 per appdatabase copies
Generated, not hand-writtenThe Better Auth CLI generates these tables from the plugin list. Physical names may change with usePlural or modelName options. This page uses the default model names from the 1.7.19 source. S1

Core tables: who the user is and how they sign in

A user has many accounts (one per sign-in method: password, Google) and many sessions (one per signed-in browser). Magic link creates no account row. It signs in against user.email directly. S6

OAuth tables: external apps, their APIs, and issued tokens

oauthClient is one external app. oauthResource is one API that tokens can be issued for, and oauthClientResource links the two. Tokens and consents point back to the client, the user and the session that produced them. S2S10

oauthClient: one registered external app (35 columns, main ones shown) S2

ColumnTypeRequiredMeaning / notes
idstringyes
clientIdstringyesUnique public id sent as client_id
clientSecretstringnoEmpty for public clients (SPA, mobile)
redirectUrisstring[]yesAllowed callback URLs
postLogoutRedirectUrisstring[]noUsed by end-session
grantTypes / responseTypesstring[]noFor example authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials
scopesstring[]noScopes the client may request for users
clientCredentialsScopesstring[]noScopes allowed for the client-credentials grant
requirePKCE / skipConsent / disabled / enableEndSessionbooleannoPer-client switches
tokenEndpointAuthMethod / applicationTypestringnoHow the client authenticates. web / native
userIdstring → user.idnoOwner, if the client was created by a user
name / uri / icon / tos / policy / contactsstringnoShown on the consent page
metadatajsonnoFree-form

Things to know before writing migrations

  1. Deleting a user cascades to its session and account rows. OAuth tokens keep the row but lose sessionId (set null). S1S2
  2. Email verification tokens are not stored. They are signed JWTs, so there is no row to clean up. S14
  3. Expired rows pile up in verification, session, oauthRefreshToken and rateLimit. Plan a daily clean-up job, which is the most a Hobby cron allows. S15 INFERRED (whether Better Auth already prunes some of these was not checked)
  4. Array columns (string[]) are mapped by the Drizzle adapter for Postgres. Check the generated schema rather than assuming a column type. OPEN
